back: A transaction is left out of the books completely. The trial balance still agrees.
An entry is made in the wrong account of the same class, for example an expense debited to another expense account.
An entry is made in the wrong class of account, for example a capital item treated as an expense.
The wrong amount is used for both the debit and the credit entries.
The right accounts are used but the debit and credit sides are swapped. The correction is twice the amount.
Two or more errors with equal and opposite effects, so the totals still agree.

front: Errors that upset the trial balance
back: One-sided entries, unequal debit and credit amounts, addition errors and wrongly copied or omitted balances.

front: Capital item treated as an expense
back: Profit is understated and non-current assets are understated. Correct by debiting the asset and crediting the expense.

front: Do errors between two expense accounts change profit?
back: No. Total expenses and therefore profit are unchanged.
